stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{4 (-1)^{n} \left(x + 4\right)^{n}}{n^{2} 6^{n}} \), whose interval of convergence is \( -10 \le x \le 2 \). Find the series for f prime obtained by term-by-term differentiation, and give the interval on which it converges.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate each term: the derivative of \( \frac{4 (-1)^{n} \left(x + 4\right)^{n}}{n^{2} 6^{n}} \) is \( \frac{4 (-1)^{n} \left(x + 4\right)^{n-1}}{n \cdot 6^{n}} \), so \( f^{\prime}(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{4 (-1)^{n} \left(x + 4\right)^{n-1}}{n \cdot 6^{n}} \).
Term-by-term differentiation keeps the radius of convergence, so the radius is still \( 6 \) and the series converges for \( \left|x + 4\right| < 6 \).

The endpoints must be checked again. At the endpoint where the terms keep one sign, the series is \( \sum \frac{4 }{6 n} \), a multiple of the harmonic series, which diverges. At the other endpoint the terms alternate and decrease to 0, so it converges by the alternating series test.
The series for f prime converges for \( -10 < x \le 2 \).

options.label: \( f^{\prime}(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{4 (-1)^{n} \left(x + 4\right)^{n-1}}{n \cdot 6^{n}} \), converging for \( -10 \le x \le 2 \).
options.derivation: the interval of f carried over with both endpoints, the endpoints of the new series never tested

options.label: \( f^{\prime}(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{4 (-1)^{n} \left(x + 4\right)^{n-1}}{n \cdot 6^{n}} \), converging for \( -10 < x < 2 \).
options.derivation: the alternating endpoint series tested with the p-series test, whose positive-terms condition it fails, and so excluded

options.label: \( f^{\prime}(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{4 (-1)^{n} \left(x + 4\right)^{n}}{n \cdot 6^{n}} \), converging for \( -10 < x \le 2 \).
options.derivation: each coefficient divided by n but the power of the displacement left at n instead of lowered to n - 1
